title: Sequence
description: Orchestration written as an async function, run on a scene's clock. ```ts const intro = new Sequence(async context => { await context.run(panToBoss); await context.all([roar, shake]); await context.wait(0.3); await context.waitUntil(() => confirm.pressed); }); const run = intro.start(this); // in a scene run.cancel(); // skip ``` A sequence is a reusable description; each start is an independent run with its own clock, steps and cleanups, and leaves nothing behind once it ends. Frame hooks stay synchronous: an `await` suspends only the sequence, and a body continues after the frame in which what it awaited completed, never inside a frame hook. Every wait completes on a tick of the run's clock, which is the scene's own time under the SequenceOptions.when policy - never wall-clock time. The scene owns its runs: ending the scene cancels them. Cancelling a run cancels every step in it, runs their cleanups, and rejects their pending waits with an `AbortError`, so `finally` blocks and SequenceContext.defer restore whatever the sequence took over. A completion that arrives after a step ended is ignored.

members.name: start
members.description: Start a run in scene, which must be attached to an application. A scene that is still being prepared holds the run's clock until it activates; one whose teardown has begun gets a run that is already cancelled.
